intro: This reference explains how English expresses numbers, dates, times, and common measurement units. It also includes conversion factors for a built-in converter.

numberSections.title: Cardinal numbers
numberSections.intro: Cardinal numbers show how many things there are.

entries.example: I work five days a week.
There are seven days in a week.
There are eleven players on the team.
There are sixteen cups in a gallon.
You can vote at eighteen in many countries.
There are twenty chairs in the room.
The room holds one hundred people.

numberSections.title: Ordinal numbers
numberSections.intro: Ordinal numbers show position or order.

numberSections.title: Large numbers
numberSections.intro: Large number names in modern short-scale English.

entries.example: The stadium holds several thousand fans.
The city has over one million residents.

entries.explanation: one thousand millions in short scale
entries.example: The company is worth two billion dollars.
entries.note: In modern English, billion usually means 1,000,000,000.

entries.explanation: one thousand billions in short scale
entries.example: The national debt reached one trillion.
The arena seats ten thousand people.
The city has a hundred thousand residents.

numberSections.title: Fractions, decimals, and math
numberSections.intro: Common ways to read fractions, decimals, percentages, and arithmetic.

entries.example: A quarter of the class was absent.
One third of the cake is left.

entries.explanation: a number written with a decimal point
a number out of one hundred
entries.example: About 20 percent of students were late.
Minus five is a negative number.

entries.explanation: the sign for subtraction or negative values
the sign or word for multiplication

entries.example: Twelve divided by three equals four.

entries.explanation: shows that two amounts are the same

entries.example: Two thirds of the students agreed.
Three quarters of the work is done.
The walk took one and a half hours.

entries.explanation: an amount expressed as part of 100
entries.example: The percentage of errors was low.
Mix water and juice in a 2:1 ratio.

entries.explanation: a number that multiplies by itself to give another number
entries.example: The square root of nine is three.

numberSections.title: Dates, time, and Roman numerals
numberSections.intro: Common number formats for dates, time, and Roman numerals.

entries.explanation: letters used in an ancient number system
a numbered day in a month and year
the hour and minutes of the day
twelve o’clock in the middle of the day

entries.example: The class starts at half past nine.

unitSections.title: SI base units
unitSections.intro: The seven base units of the International System of Units (SI).

entries.name: metre
entries.definition: the SI base unit of length
entries.example: The room is four metres wide.

entries.name: kilogram
entries.definition: the SI base unit of mass

entries.name: second
entries.definition: the SI base unit of time

entries.name: ampere
entries.definition: the SI base unit of electric current

entries.name: kelvin
entries.definition: the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature

entries.name: mole
entries.definition: the SI base unit for amount of substance

entries.name: candela
entries.definition: the SI base unit of luminous intensity
entries.example: The lamp has a luminous intensity measured in candelas.

unitSections.title: Common SI derived units
unitSections.intro: Important SI derived units used in everyday science and technology.

entries.name: newton
entries.definition: the SI unit of force
entries.example: The force was measured in newtons.

entries.name: joule
entries.definition: the SI unit of energy and work
entries.example: Food energy can be compared in joules.

entries.name: watt
entries.definition: the SI unit of power

entries.name: pascal
entries.definition: the SI unit of pressure
entries.example: Tire pressure is often given in kilopascals.

entries.name: hertz
entries.definition: the SI unit of frequency
entries.example: The note has a frequency of 440 hertz.

entries.name: volt
entries.definition: the SI unit of electric potential difference

entries.name: degree Celsius
entries.definition: a temperature scale used in most countries

unitSections.title: SI prefixes
unitSections.intro: Prefixes that scale SI units by powers of ten.

entries.name: kilo
entries.definition: a prefix meaning one thousand

entries.name: hecto
entries.definition: a prefix meaning one hundred

entries.name: deca
entries.definition: a prefix meaning ten

entries.name: deci
entries.definition: a prefix meaning one tenth

entries.name: centi
entries.definition: a prefix meaning one hundredth

entries.name: milli
entries.definition: a prefix meaning one thousandth

entries.name: micro
entries.definition: a prefix meaning one millionth
entries.example: A microsecond is one millionth of a second.

entries.name: mega
entries.definition: a prefix meaning one million
entries.example: One megabyte is often used informally for digital size.

entries.name: giga
entries.definition: a prefix meaning one billion
entries.example: A gigawatt is one billion watts.

unitSections.title: Length units
unitSections.intro: Common metric, imperial, and nautical length units.

entries.name: kilometre
entries.definition: a metric unit of length equal to 1,000 metres
entries.example: The village is five kilometres away.

entries.name: centimetre
entries.definition: a metric unit of length equal to 0.01 metre

entries.name: millimetre
entries.definition: a metric unit of length equal to 0.001 metre
entries.example: The gap is two millimetres wide.

entries.name: mile
entries.definition: an imperial/US unit of length equal to 1,609.344 metres
entries.example: The park is two miles away.

entries.name: yard
entries.definition: an imperial/US unit of length equal to 0.9144 metre
entries.example: The fabric is three yards long.

entries.name: foot
entries.definition: an imperial/US unit of length equal to 0.3048 metre

entries.name: inch
entries.definition: an imperial/US unit of length equal to 0.0254 metre

entries.name: nautical mile
entries.definition: a unit used in sea and air travel equal to 1,852 metres

entries.name: micrometre
entries.definition: a metric unit equal to one millionth of a metre
entries.example: A human hair is about 70 micrometres thick.

entries.name: nanometre
entries.definition: a metric unit equal to one billionth of a metre
entries.example: DNA is about two nanometres wide.

unitSections.title: Mass units
unitSections.intro: Common metric and imperial units of mass.

entries.name: gram
entries.definition: a metric unit of mass equal to 0.001 kilogram

entries.name: milligram
entries.definition: a metric unit of mass equal to 0.000001 kilogram

entries.name: tonne
entries.definition: a metric unit of mass equal to 1,000 kilograms

entries.name: pound
entries.definition: an imperial/US unit of mass equal to 0.45359237 kilogram

entries.name: ounce
entries.definition: an imperial/US unit of mass equal to 0.028349523125 kilogram

entries.name: stone
entries.definition: a British unit of mass equal to 6.35029318 kilograms

entries.name: carat
entries.definition: a unit of mass used for gemstones, equal to 200 milligrams

entries.name: metric ton
entries.definition: another name for tonne, equal to 1,000 kilograms
entries.example: The shipment weighed three metric tons.

unitSections.title: Volume and capacity
unitSections.intro: Common volume units for science, daily life, and cooking.

entries.name: litre
entries.definition: a metric unit of volume equal to 0.001 cubic metre

entries.name: millilitre
entries.definition: a metric unit of volume equal to 0.000001 cubic metre

entries.name: cubic metre
entries.definition: the SI unit of volume
entries.example: The tank holds two cubic metres.

entries.name: US gallon
entries.definition: a US unit of liquid volume equal to 3.785411784 litres
entries.example: The car uses a gallon of fuel.

entries.name: UK gallon
entries.definition: a British unit of volume equal to 4.54609 litres
entries.example: The old recipe used a UK gallon.

entries.name: pint
entries.definition: a unit of volume; different in UK and US
entries.example: He ordered a pint of juice.
entries.note: US pint used as default factor; see note.

entries.name: cup
entries.definition: a cooking volume measure, often 240 mL in US recipes

entries.name: tablespoon
entries.definition: a cooking measure equal to about 15 mL

entries.name: teaspoon
entries.definition: a cooking measure equal to about 5 mL

unitSections.title: Area units
unitSections.intro: Units used to measure surface area.

entries.name: square metre
entries.definition: the SI unit of area

entries.name: square kilometre
entries.definition: an area equal to 1,000,000 square metres

entries.name: hectare
entries.definition: an area equal to 10,000 square metres
entries.example: The farm has 20 hectares of land.

entries.name: acre
entries.definition: an imperial/US unit of area equal to 4,046.8564224 square metres
entries.example: They bought five acres of land.

entries.name: square foot
entries.definition: an area equal to 0.09290304 square metre

entries.name: square mile
entries.definition: an area equal to 2,589,988.110336 square metres

entries.name: square inch
entries.definition: an area equal to 0.00064516 square metre
entries.example: The label is four square inches.

unitSections.title: Speed units
unitSections.intro: Units used to measure speed in transport and science.

entries.name: metre per second
entries.definition: the SI unit of speed
entries.example: The runner moved at five metres per second.

entries.name: kilometre per hour
entries.definition: a speed unit common in transport
entries.example: The speed limit is 50 kilometres per hour.

entries.name: mile per hour
entries.definition: an imperial/US speed unit
entries.example: The car was going 60 miles per hour.

entries.name: knot
entries.definition: a nautical speed unit equal to one nautical mile per hour

entries.name: minute
entries.definition: a unit of time equal to 60 seconds

entries.name: hour
entries.definition: a unit of time equal to 60 minutes

entries.name: day
entries.definition: a unit of time equal to 24 hours

entries.name: week
entries.definition: a unit of time equal to seven days

entries.name: year
entries.definition: a unit of time equal to about 365 days
entries.example: She lived abroad for one year.

unitSections.title: Temperature units
unitSections.intro: Common temperature scales and conversion notes.

entries.name: degree Celsius
entries.definition: a temperature scale where water freezes at 0 and boils at 100

entries.name: degree Fahrenheit
entries.definition: a temperature scale used mainly in the United States

entries.name: kelvin
entries.definition: an absolute temperature scale used in science

unitSections.title: Digital storage units
unitSections.intro: Units used for files, memory, and storage.

entries.name: bit
entries.definition: the smallest unit of digital information

entries.name: byte
entries.definition: a unit of digital information equal to 8 bits

entries.name: kilobyte
entries.definition: about one thousand bytes; sometimes 1,024 bytes in binary use
entries.note: Binary systems may use kibibyte (1024 bytes).

entries.name: megabyte
entries.definition: about one million bytes

entries.name: gigabyte
entries.definition: about one billion bytes
entries.example: The phone has 128 gigabytes of storage.

entries.name: terabyte
entries.definition: about one trillion bytes

entries.name: kibibyte
entries.definition: a binary unit equal to 1,024 bytes
entries.example: The file size is shown as 4 kibibytes.

entries.name: mebibyte
entries.definition: a binary unit equal to 1,048,576 bytes

unitSections.title: Angle units
unitSections.intro: Units used to measure angles and rotation.

entries.name: degree
entries.definition: a unit of angle equal to 1/360 of a full turn

entries.name: radian
entries.definition: the SI unit of angle
entries.example: A full circle is 2 pi radians.

unitSections.title: Energy and power units
unitSections.intro: Common units for energy in science and daily life.

entries.name: calorie
entries.definition: a small unit of energy; in food, kilocalories are often called calories
entries.example: The label shows energy in calories.

entries.name: kilocalorie
entries.definition: a unit of energy equal to 1,000 calories

entries.name: kilowatt-hour
entries.definition: a unit of energy used for electricity bills
entries.example: The house used 300 kilowatt-hours this month.

entries.name: electronvolt
entries.definition: a very small energy unit used in physics
entries.example: Particle energies are measured in electronvolts.

unitSections.title: Pressure units
unitSections.intro: Units used for air, tires, and scientific pressure.

entries.name: bar
entries.definition: a metric pressure unit equal to 100,000 pascals

entries.name: pounds per square inch
entries.definition: an imperial/US pressure unit

entries.name: atmosphere
entries.definition: a pressure unit close to average sea-level air pressure

unitSections.title: Cooking measures
unitSections.intro: Common measures used in recipes. Units vary by country.

entries.name: pinch
entries.definition: a very small amount held between finger and thumb

entries.name: dash
entries.definition: a very small liquid amount

entries.name: fluid ounce
entries.definition: a liquid volume unit; US 29.5735 mL, UK 28.4131 mL
entries.example: Add eight fluid ounces of water.
entries.note: US value used as default factor.

entries.name: quart
entries.definition: a unit equal to two pints

unitSections.title: Nautical and astronomical units
unitSections.intro: Units used for sea travel and space distances.

entries.name: fathom
entries.definition: a nautical unit of depth equal to 1.8288 metres
entries.example: The water was ten fathoms deep.

entries.name: league
entries.definition: a historical distance unit, often about 4.828 kilometres
entries.example: The ship was many leagues away.

entries.name: astronomical unit
entries.definition: the average distance from Earth to the Sun
entries.example: Mars is about 1.5 astronomical units from the Sun.

entries.name: light-year
entries.definition: the distance light travels in one year
entries.example: The star is four light-years away.

phrases.example: I bought a pair of shoes.
She bought half a dozen rolls.
I will be there in a couple of minutes.
Hundreds of people attended the festival.
The answer is two point five.

phrases.meaning: two times as much or as many

phrases.example: One in ten people preferred the new design.

phrases.meaning: a whole number not divisible by 2
